clue.text: Prophet has to do without a pipe

indicators.note: to do without something is to manage with it gone, so the letter named is dropped from the prophet

parts.note: Hosea is an Old Testament prophet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prophet must manage without a pipe for his tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' sounds like smoking gear, but it is a garden or fire pipe; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hose is a flexible tube carrying water, a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Held in a coil, end of the streamer, perhaps

indicators.note: letters held in a coil are twisted round into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from the word the

explanation.surface: Held in a coil, the end of a paper streamer perhaps curls up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coil' rearranges HELDINA into HEADLIN; the end of 'the' adds E. 'Streamer' is not party decoration but a banner across a newspaper page.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a streamer is a large title running across the whole width of a page.

clue.text: Having for sale an example of 1 ac.

definitions.meaning: a shop ... an item keeps it to sell
1 across is the hose worn on the leg, and one item of hosiery is a long knitted leg covering

explanation.definitionFit: Stocking is both carrying goods for sale and a type of hosiery worn on the leg.

clue.text: Everything husband owns on November Ist

parts.note: all means everything
to own up is to admit, and to allow can mean to admit or acknowledge

explanation.surface: Everything a husband possesses is listed for the first of November.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints '1st'; the OCR shows it as 'Ist'. 'Owns' here means admits, as in owning a fault, matching 'allows'.
explanation.definitionFit: All Saints' Day, the feast of all the saints, falls on the first of November and has this older name.

clue.text: Longbow's structure made of wood

parts.note: the long of longbow gives L, the usual abbreviation for long
a bow is a curved structure, an arch

explanation.surface: An archer's longbow is described as being made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Split longbow into long bow: long gives L and the bow's curved structure is an ARCH. 'Made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose tough timber is a common wood.

clue.text: Cramp the style of bad actors supported by Herts town

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts badly
Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire (Herts), an English county north of London

explanation.surface: Poor actors cramp a production backed by a Hertfordshire town's money.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple or hamper them, limiting what they can do.

clue.text: Around beginning of term, the head girl is skittish and carefree

indicators.note: letters turned around are put in another order, the first anagram signal here
skittish letters jump about restlessly, rearranging the fodder
the beginning of the word term is its first letter

explanation.surface: Around the start of term, the head girl of a school is frisky and carefree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' and 'skittish' both signal the anagram of T (from 'term') plus THE HEAD GIRL; 'is' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being light-hearted means cheerful and untroubled, without worries.

clue.text: Rounds including wine — from here?

indicators.note: one piece including another holds it inside

parts.note: two round shapes are two letters O
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Rounds of drinks include wine; does it come from this place?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: port wine takes its name from this Portuguese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto (Porto) is the city in Portugal that ships port and gave the wine its name.

clue.text: Uncompromising English novelist

parts.note: stern means strict and unyielding

explanation.surface: A hardline English writer of fiction refuses to compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century author of the novel Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Hail a boat

parts.note: taken as written
a hoy is a heavy barge or small coastal vessel

explanation.surface: Call out to a passing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail a boat' reads as the definition, but only 'Hail' defines; a hoy is an old type of barge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use this cry to greet or call to another vessel.

clue.text: Removing old shrubs and trees in Midland town

indicators.note: removing one piece from another takes it out

parts.note: broom is a yellow-flowered shrub, and brooms are several
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: Clearing out old bushes and trees in a town in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing' takes O out of BROOMS, leaving BROMS. Bromsgrove is a market town in Worcestershire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromsgrove is a town in Worcestershire, a county in central England known as the Midlands.

clue.text: Cross about intelligence involving large vessel

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: one piece involving another wraps around it

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
a tanker is a large ship carrying oil

explanation.surface: Someone angry about spy intelligence concerning a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is an adjective meaning angry, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous describes someone bad-tempered and quarrelsome, an angry sort.

clue.text: Instantly looking round, in field event?

definitions.meaning: resembling the round iron ball thrown in the shot put athletics event

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at once, and literally it means resembling the heavy ball put in athletics.

clue.text: Prometheus, for instance, got it, and was forsaken by god

indicators.note: something forsaken by another is abandoned by it, so those letters leave

parts.note: these words lose G, O and D; that the remaining letters also run unbroken inside them is a coincidence, not a hidden-word device
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prometheus stole fire and was abandoned by the gods to punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of GOT IT AND and strike out G, O and D in order, as the god forsakes them.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Prometheus was one of the Titans, the giant older gods.

clue.text: Still in ignorance, group of players is restricted by one making cuts

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

indicators.note: a piece restricted by another is hemmed in by it

parts.note: a hewer chops wood or coal

explanation.surface: Still unaware, a band is held back by a man cutting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of players' suggests a team, but a nonet here is a nine-piece musical ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who still knows no more than before.

clue.text: Watch the first batsman carefully — it might be revealing

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it, carefully in the surface
in cricket the opener is a batsman who goes in first

explanation.surface: Keep a close watch on the opening batsman, who may show something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carefully' belongs with 'Watch' to support EYE, to look at closely. In cricket the opener bats first.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprising discovery or revelation shows the truth and so opens one's understanding.

clue.text: Support socialist's thrash

parts.note: to be for a side is to support it, as in 'be Labour' meaning to back the party
Labour is the British socialist party

explanation.surface: Back a left-wing politician's beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Support socialist' as BE LABOUR, to side with Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour is to beat or attack someone, physically or with words.

clue.text: Cut what college produces?

definitions.meaning: the harvest grown by Eton College, read as its produce

explanation.definitionFit: An Eton crop is a short women's haircut of the 1920s; read literally it is the produce of Eton College.

clue.text: Clothing ragmen turned out

indicators.note: letters put out are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rag-and-bone men have turned some clothes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'out' rearranges RAGMEN TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: An item worn beneath outer clothes, such as a vest, is a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Money scholar's hidden inside citadel

indicators.note: a piece hidden inside another sits within it

parts.note: cash is money
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar's degree, standing for the scholar

explanation.surface: A scholar's money is stashed in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scholar's' means scholar is, so the scholar is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the fortress or old walled quarter of a North African city.

clue.text: Trouble experienced lifting plant

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting reads the pieces upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
had means experienced, as in had a good time

explanation.surface: Someone had difficulty heaving up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns AILHAD to read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower with large showy blooms.

clue.text: One can get around Pennsylvania quickly

indicators.note: a piece that gets around another surrounds it

parts.note: an ace is the one in cards or dice
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: One person can travel around Pennsylvania fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old word for at speed or swiftly.

clue.text: Crockery in place or out of place?

indicators.note: letters out of place are moved into another order

explanation.surface: Is a china set laid in its place, or out of place?
explanation.definitionFit: Fine china dishes and plates are made of this ceramic.

clue.text: Knight brought in to break up quarrel

indicators.note: one piece brought in to another is set inside it

parts.note: to ruin something is to wreck or break it
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is called in to break up a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an argument or clash with someone.

clue.text: Sport that is expanding

definitions.meaning: a leisure pursuit, here flying in hot-air craft

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the pastime of hot-air flight and swelling up in size.

clue.text: Someone like Othello needed opportunity to reflect

indicators.note: a reflection shows a word mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: room means scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: Othello needed a chance to reflect on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello, in Shakespeare's play, is a Moor, a North African Muslim.

clue.text: The dragon's unusually pigheaded

indicators.note: something done unusually is out of its normal order

parts.note: the letters of the dragon's, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: The dragon is unusually stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'dragon's' is part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Headstrong means stubborn and wilful, refusing to be advised.

clue.text: Slip up as a result of drug-taking

definitions.meaning: to stumble or make an error
a hallucinatory experience brought on by drugs such as LSD

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to stumble or blunder and an hallucinogenic drug experience.
